catalog_quote: Data showing the stress-final patterns in words with a reconstructed Schwa penult are included below in (4). ... Other languages where these patterns have been reported include at least Pangasinan, Balangaw, Isnag, Ibanag, Central Cagayan Agta, Ifugao (see Blust and Trussel ongoing; Healey 1960; Reid 1971), Northern Subanan (Daguman 2013: 47), Sarangani Manobo (DuBois 1976) Sangil (Sneddon 1984: 24) and Tiruray (Schlegel 1971: 7). All Philippine language data discussed so far show stress-shift to the final syllable after a penultimate schwa. [Blust 2013: 179] the tendency to lose contrastive stress becomes increasingly clearer south of the Bisayas. In almost all languages of Mindanao stress is penultimate (Subanen, Manobo, Danaw languages), or final (Bilic languages).

Only differences: the report's quote joins two sources -- the Smith sentences, then an editorial bracket "[Supporting survey, Blust 2013: 179:]" followed by the Blust sentence, which is itself verbatim in Blust 2013 printed p.179, p.221: "In almost all languages of Mindanao stress is penultimate (Subanen, Manobo, Danaw languages), or final (Bi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand only: primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable, non-contrastively, except that it shifts to the final syllable when the penult contains a schwa (Smith 2023 reporting Daguman 2013: 47). Blust 2013 independently groups Subanen with the Mindanao languages that have lost contrastive stress and are regularly penultimate.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa penult repels stress to the final syllable (per Smith 2023 citing Daguman 2013: 47). No further detail (loanwords, closed penults, clitics) available second-hand.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement as reported; Smith's context is the historical stress-shift pattern (*CəCVC roots), not a full synchronic description. Lobel 2013: 313-314 notes that Subanen phrases 'sound like single phonological words', so the word/phrase domain in Northern Subanen is unverified until Daguman 2013 ch. on phonology is read.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern Northern Subanen [stb] = nort2885 (Daguman's data from Katipunan/Dipolog/Polanco area, Zamboanga del Norte; Wikipedia/Ethnologue alt names Tuboy Subanon, Salug-Godod Subanen). Smith 2023 spells it 'Northern Subanan' but cites Daguman 2013 A grammar of Northern Subanen. Blust 2013's 'Subanen' is the group, not a specific variety. Sister-language first-hand statements exist held by the project for Central/Sindangan Subanen [syb] cent2089 (Brichoux 1977: no contrastive word stress) and must not be attributed to nort2885.
